workflows.title: Build an authorization package
workflows.summary: Turn the governing program's requirements into a traceable package inventory, system description, implementation record, assessment set, and remediation record.

steps.title: Choose the governing path
steps.action: Identify the authorizing program, impact or baseline, system boundary, and current rules before selecting documents.
steps.completion_signal: The package owner can name the authority, rule set, boundary, and submission channel.

steps.title: Create the package manifest
steps.action: List every required artifact, its official source, owner, status, dependencies, and delivery format.
steps.completion_signal: Every required artifact is present, intentionally not applicable, or assigned with a due date.

steps.title: Build and assess the evidence chain
steps.action: Connect control implementation statements to evidence, assessment procedures, findings, and remediation records.
steps.completion_signal: Each selected control has an implementation source, assessment status, and traceable result.

readiness_checks: All artifacts identify their governing source and version.
Legacy documents are visibly marked and reconciled to current rules.
The package has owners, dates, and evidence locations.
Machine-readable artifacts validate against the pinned schema version.
workflows.boundary_note: Control Atlas can organize and structurally validate package material; only the authorized program and authorizing officials determine acceptance.

workflows.title: Write control implementation statements
workflows.summary: Translate selected requirements into specific, testable descriptions of who performs each safeguard, what they do, where it operates, and what proves it.

steps.title: Resolve the requirement
steps.action: Read the control statement, parameters, enhancements, implementation guidance, and inherited responsibility before drafting.
steps.completion_signal: The writer can explain the exact obligation and which part applies locally.

steps.title: Describe the operating safeguard
steps.action: Record responsible roles, mechanisms, scope, frequency, dependencies, and exceptions in testable language.
steps.completion_signal: An assessor can identify what to examine, interview, or test.

steps.title: Attach evidence and ownership
steps.action: Link each assertion to evidence type, location, custodian, review cadence, and freshness expectation.
steps.completion_signal: Every material assertion has an owner and an evidence path.

readiness_checks: Statements are system-specific rather than control restatements.
Inherited and local responsibilities are separated.
Evidence can be collected without guessing what the statement means.
workflows.boundary_note: Schema alignment can validate structure but cannot prove that an implementation is effective.

workflows.title: Prepare for a security assessment
workflows.summary: Define scope, procedures, targets, evidence, assessors, timing, and result handling before testing begins.

steps.title: Set scope and authority
steps.action: Name the assessment driver, control set, system boundary, components, locations, exclusions, and assessment period.
steps.completion_signal: The owner and assessor agree on what is and is not being evaluated.

steps.title: Map procedures to evidence
steps.action: Assign examine, interview, and test procedures with targets, evidence owners, collection dates, and dependencies.
steps.completion_signal: Every in-scope objective has a method, owner, and evidence request.

steps.title: Define result handling
steps.action: Agree on result identifiers, severity or risk treatment, retest rules, report format, and POA&M handoff.
steps.completion_signal: A finding can move from test result to report and remediation without manual re-identification.

readiness_checks: Scope, methods, dates, assessors, and targets are recorded.
Evidence requests have owners and secure delivery paths.
Result identifiers will remain stable across reports and remediation.
workflows.boundary_note: A structurally ready plan is not approval to begin testing; obtain the required authorization and coordination.

workflows.title: Run and document a STIG assessment
workflows.summary: Select the correct STIG, collect automated and manual results, preserve target identity, and produce a validated checklist handoff.

steps.title: Choose the benchmark and target
steps.action: Confirm product, version, benchmark release, target hostname, addresses, role, and applicability before evaluating rules.
steps.completion_signal: The checklist identifies one unambiguous target and benchmark release.

steps.title: Collect and reconcile results
steps.action: Import supported automated results, complete manual checks, document finding details and comments, and review not-applicable decisions.
steps.completion_signal: Every applicable rule has a reviewed status and adequate finding detail.

steps.title: Validate the handoff
steps.action: Open the output in the named STIG Viewer release, resolve validation warnings, and preserve the original plus reviewed export.
steps.completion_signal: The output imports cleanly and round-trips without losing target or rule data.

readiness_checks: Benchmark and target versions are explicit.
Automated results were reviewed instead of accepted blindly.
Manual checks and not-applicable rationales are complete.
The final file passed tool validation and round-trip review.
workflows.boundary_note: A generated CSV or checklist is only compatible after validation in the named receiving tool; it is not an authorization decision.

workflows.title: Create or update a POA&M
workflows.summary: Turn confirmed weaknesses into owned, dated, traceable remediation work with milestones, risk context, and closure evidence.

steps.title: Normalize the weakness
steps.action: Assign a stable identifier and record the source, affected assets, controls, detection date, severity, and risk basis.
steps.completion_signal: The weakness can be traced back to its source result without text matching.

steps.title: Plan measurable remediation
steps.action: Name the owner, resources, scheduled completion, dependencies, and milestones with dates and observable completion criteria.
steps.completion_signal: Each open item has a current owner and at least one measurable path to closure.

steps.title: Validate status and closure
steps.action: Reconcile milestone status, document delay or risk acceptance decisions, retest fixes, and attach closure evidence.
steps.completion_signal: Closed items contain independent retest or accepted closure evidence.

readiness_checks: Identifiers remain stable across source, POA&M, and retest records.
Milestones contain dates and completion criteria.
Late items explain impact and next action.
Closed items include closure evidence.
workflows.boundary_note: Historical workbook similarity or eMASS API schema alignment is not proof that a workbook can be imported into a target eMASS instance.

workflows.title: Establish hardware and software baselines
workflows.summary: Create owned, reviewable inventories that connect components and software to authorization boundaries, versions, locations, and lifecycle decisions.

steps.title: Define the inventory boundary
steps.action: State which environments, components, software classes, virtual assets, and external services are included.
steps.completion_signal: Operators know what must appear and what is managed elsewhere.

steps.title: Normalize asset records
steps.action: Use stable identifiers and record manufacturer or publisher, model or product, version, role, location, owner, status, and authorization-boundary relationship.
steps.completion_signal: Records can be compared over time without relying on display names alone.

steps.title: Connect changes and reviews
steps.action: Set review cadence, evidence source, change-log linkage, end-of-support tracking, and reconciliation ownership.
steps.completion_signal: A reviewer can explain who updates the baseline and how changes are detected.

readiness_checks: All records belong to the declared boundary.
Required identifiers, versions, owners, and status fields are present.
Baseline review and reconciliation dates are recorded.
workflows.boundary_note: A Control Atlas baseline can prepare schema-aligned data but does not replace an official system-generated import or the configuration-management system of record.

workflows.title: Prepare PPSM information
workflows.summary: Collect application, protocol, port, service, boundary, mission, and implementation data before working in the official PPSM process.

steps.title: Identify declared services
steps.action: List applications, protocols, ports, services, direction, endpoints, environments, and mission owners.
steps.completion_signal: Each service is connected to a system, mission use, and network path.

steps.title: Document implementation and risk context
steps.action: Record boundary devices, allowed flows, applicable STIGs, discovery evidence, nonstandard use, and exception needs.
steps.completion_signal: Reviewers can distinguish standard, nonstandard, and exception-dependent use.

steps.title: Complete the official registry workflow
steps.action: Use current component procedures and the authenticated PPSM Registry to validate and submit the prepared data.
steps.completion_signal: The official system records the declaration or returns actionable corrections.

readiness_checks: Every PPS has an owner and mission purpose.
Endpoints, direction, protocol, port, and service details are complete.
Exceptions and nonstandard use are identified before submission.
workflows.boundary_note: No public blank PPSM Registry import template was verified. A Control Atlas worksheet is preparation material, not an official registry artifact.

workflows.title: Organize continuous monitoring deliverables
workflows.summary: Translate monitoring obligations into a recurring calendar of evidence, reports, owners, review points, and escalation actions.

steps.title: Identify monitoring obligations
steps.action: List recurring and event-driven deliverables from current rules, authorization conditions, and organizational policy.
steps.completion_signal: Every obligation has a trigger, cadence, due date rule, and recipient.

steps.title: Assign collection and review
steps.action: Name the producer, reviewer, evidence source, secure location, validation method, and escalation owner.
steps.completion_signal: A missed or invalid deliverable has an obvious next owner and action.

steps.title: Validate each reporting cycle
steps.action: Check completeness, reporting period, change summaries, vulnerabilities, incidents, exceptions, and delivery confirmation.
steps.completion_signal: The cycle is structurally complete and all unresolved exceptions are assigned.

readiness_checks: Current rules take precedence over the legacy calendar.
Dates, owners, evidence sources, reviewers, and recipients are present.
Machine-readable reports validate against their dated schema.
workflows.boundary_note: Calendar completion is not proof that monitoring evidence is adequate or accepted.

workflows.title: Evaluate inheritance and shared responsibility
workflows.summary: Separate provider, common-control, customer, and system responsibilities and retain the evidence needed to rely on inherited safeguards.

steps.title: Collect the responsibility sources
steps.action: Obtain current provider matrices, common-control packages, service descriptions, secure-configuration guidance, and customer agreements.
steps.completion_signal: Every claimed inherited responsibility has a named, dated source.

steps.title: Allocate each requirement
steps.action: Classify responsibility as inherited, shared, local, or not applicable and record provider evidence plus required customer implementation.
steps.completion_signal: Shared controls describe both parties' actions rather than using a generic inherited label.

steps.title: Resolve freshness and gaps
steps.action: Check source currency, authorization scope, service tier, region, and local deviations; assign unresolved responsibilities.
steps.completion_signal: No inherited claim depends on stale, out-of-scope, or unavailable evidence without an explicit decision.

readiness_checks: Responsibility source, version, and date are recorded.
Shared responsibilities state both provider and customer actions.
Local deltas and missing evidence have owners.
workflows.boundary_note: A legacy CRM is a structural reference only; use the provider's current responsibility material for an actual inheritance decision.

workflows.title: Prepare a package for reciprocity review
workflows.summary: Determine whether an existing authorization package can reduce duplicate assessment work by testing scope, freshness, evidence, and residual gaps.

steps.title: Understand the source authorization
steps.action: Record authorizing organization, decision date, boundary, baseline, conditions, expiration or review cycle, and package access.
steps.completion_signal: The reviewer can state exactly what was authorized and under which conditions.

steps.title: Test completeness and freshness
steps.action: Review the SSP, assessment report, POA&M, continuous-monitoring evidence, changes, and inherited-control sources for currency and accessibility.
steps.completion_signal: Reusable material and stale or missing material are separately identified.

steps.title: Bound the delta assessment
steps.action: Compare target environment, mission, data, interconnections, threats, overlays, and risk tolerance; assign only the evidence or testing needed for material differences.
steps.completion_signal: The accepting official has a traceable reuse recommendation and a bounded list of delta work.

readiness_checks: Source authorization scope and conditions are documented.
Package artifacts have freshness dates and access status.
Target-environment differences are tied to specific evidence or tests.
Residual risk and acceptance ownership are explicit.
workflows.boundary_note: Control Atlas can organize a reciprocity review; only the receiving authorizing organization can accept prior authorization evidence or risk.
